settings.name_in_paper: Reward (loss) poisoning attack on adversarial multi-armed bandits
unmapped: The guarantees are for an ATTACKER, not the learner: the attacker perturbs observed losses (kept in [0,1]) to force a victim no-regret bandit algorithm to pull a target arm a^dagger T-o(T) times at o(T) cumulative attack cost C_T = sum |tilde l_t - l_t|; no vocabulary objective covers this
Victim is any bandit algorithm with regret O(T^alpha_r), alpha_r in [1/2,1); attacker knows alpha_r but not the losses or the victim algorithm
settings.definition_quote: The focus of our paper is to design efficient attack algorithms that can achieve $\E{}{N_T(a^\dagger)}=T-o(T)$ and $\E{}{C_T}=o(T)$ while being \textbf{\textit{agnostic}} to the concrete victim bandit algorithms.

source.label: thm:non-maximum_target_loss
source.quote: Assume assumption~\ref{assump:easier} holds, and the attacker applies~\eqref{eq:easy_Ell} to perform attack. Then there exists a constant $M>0$ such that the expected number of target arm selections satisfies $\E{}{N_T(a^\dagger)}\ge T-MT^\alpha/\rho$, and the expected cumulative attack cost satisfies $\E{}{C_T}\le MT^\alpha/\rho$.

source.label: col:minimum_cost
source.quote: Assume the attacker applies~\eqref{eq:maximum_target_loss_Ell} to perform attack. Then when the attacker chooses $\epsilon=\frac{1-\alpha}{2}$, the expected cumulative attack cost achieves the minimum value asymptotically. Correspondingly, we have $\E{}{N_T(a^\dagger)}= T-O(T^{\frac{1+\alpha}{2}})$ and $\E{}{C_T}=O(T^{\frac{1+\alpha}{2}})$.

conditions: victim has regret O(T^alpha_r), alpha_r in [1/2,1)

source.label: thm:thmHardReoverEasy
source.quote: Let $\rho\in(0,1]$ be any constant. Define $\T_\rho=\{t\mid \Ell_t(a^\dagger)>1-\rho\}$... Let $|\T_\rho|=\tau$. ... \E{}{N_T(a^\dagger)}\ge T-\rho^{\frac{1}{\alpha+\epsilon-1}}-\tau-MT^\alpha/\rho

source.label: thm:thmHardReoverEasy
source.quote: and the cumulative attack cost satisfies \E{}{C_T}\le \rho^{\frac{1}{\alpha+\epsilon-1}}+\tau+MT^\alpha/\rho.

symbols.alpha_r: regret rate exponent of victim, in [1/2,1)

conditions: applies to victim-agnostic attackers achieving E[N_T(a^dagger)] = T - o(T) against all victims with regret O(T^alpha_r)
hard instance: K=2, losses 0 and 0.5, target is the 0.5 arm; victim Exp3 with eta = Theta(T^-alpha_r)

source.label: thm:lower_bound
source.quote: Assume some victim-agnostic attack algorithm achieves $\E{}{N_T(a^\dagger)}=T-o(T)$ on all victim bandit algorithms that has regret rate $O(T^\alpha)$, where $\alpha\in[\frac{1}{2}, 1)$. Then there exists a bandit task such that the attacker must induce at least expected attack cost $\E{}{C_T}=\Omega(T^\alpha)$ on some victim algorithm. Specifically, one such victim is the Exp3 algorithm with parameter $\eta=\Theta(T^{-\alpha})$.

results.notes: Lower bound on the attacker's cumulative cost, not on regret.
